# ring homomorphism　`def.ring-hom`
English entry · root `../`
[in graph](../#n=def.ring-hom)　·　[Chinese page (authoritative)](./def.ring-hom.md)

The **kernel** $\ker f := \{\, a \in R : f(a) = 0 \,\}$ is an **ideal** of $R$; the **image** $\operatorname{im} f$ is a subring of $S$. The map $f$ is injective if and only if $\ker f = 0$; a bijective ring homomorphism is an **isomorphism**.

## Notes · **draft**
⭐ Examples: $\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$; $K[x] \to K$, $f \mapsto f(a)$ (evaluation); $\mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$, $z \mapsto \bar z$ (conjugation, a ring isomorphism but not a $\mathbb{C}$-algebra homomorphism).
